description: Deterministic inbound screening rules (ADR-200 sections 8.3 and 8.4). Phrase terms are matched case-insensitively over whitespace-collapsed text. A rule fires when any of its terms matches. Terms written as a bracketed token (<cf>, <attachment>, <no-text-part>) select a structural matcher rather than a literal phrase.

families.hidden_text: Unicode format characters (category Cf) outside emoji sequences, or HTML text hidden from a sighted reader while the plain-text part does not carry the same words.
families.agent_addressed: Text addressed to an automated reader: instruction-override phrases, role claims, and requests to reveal or change instructions.
families.action_request: Requests to run, install or execute something, pipe a download into a shell, connect to a server or tool endpoint, or supply a credential, token or password.
families.executable_attachment: An attachment whose declared or sniffed type is executable or a script.
families.html_only: No text/plain part; the message is delivered with text extracted from the HTML.
families.opt_out: Explicit opt-out phrasing in the subject or the first non-quoted line. Drives the unsubscribe entry point and never changes the delivery outcome.

rules.description: A Unicode format (Cf) character that can hide or reorder text for a sighted reader. Emoji zero-width joiners and tag characters inside an emoji sequence are excluded.
HTML text whose style sets the display property to none, while the plain-text part does not carry the same text. The property is listed here; the value test lives in the matcher.
HTML text whose style sets the visibility property to hidden, while the plain-text part does not carry the same text.
HTML text whose style sets the font-size property to a zero length, while the plain-text part does not carry the same text.
HTML text whose colour equals its background colour, while the plain-text part does not carry the same text.
An instruction-override phrase addressed to an automated reader.
A role claim that reframes the reader as a different actor.
A request to reveal or change the reader's instructions or configuration.
A download piped into a shell.
A request to run, install or execute a command, or to connect the reader to a server or tool endpoint.
A request for the reader's own credential, token or password.
An attachment whose declared content type, file name extension, or leading bytes mark it as executable or a script (for example a PE image starting with MZ, or a #! script header).
No text/plain part; the message is delivered with text extracted from the HTML.
An explicit opt-out phrase in the subject or the first non-quoted line.
